items.problem: Two defects in one check, both of the shape this loop has now documented three times (D8, L2, and I36's own finding that a check was narrower than the rule it enforced). (a) SCOPE: S20's intent reads 'on the home page, no resting-state border uses --accent, and every sibling in a repeated list ... shares its siblings' resting border-top colour', but the check body reads borderTopColor from `.door` and `.deltas-strip .delta` only. I enumerated every element on the rendered home page carrying a non-zero border of rgb(74,59,212) on any side: `.change-annotation` carries a 2px border-LEFT in exactly that colour, at rest, and S20 is green. I judge that instance itself defensible - it marks the one annotated entry of 24 and the page names the state in its adjacent 'WHAT IT MEANS' label, which is the exception R9's own iter-08 addendum permits - so the artifact is probably right and the intent string is wrong. But a reader of the gate output is told a page-wide prohibition holds when a per-selector one was tested, and the next accent border added anywhere on that page will ship green. (b) ESCAPE HATCH: the change manifest states the gate ran '19 of 19, every check carrying falsifier evidence in both directions, zero `oneSidedBecause` escape hatches'. S20 declares `oneSidedBecause`. The string occurs three times in tools/ui-invariants.mjs - once as S20's declaration and twice inside the audit machinery at lines 1510 and 1512 - against exactly two occurrences when iter-07's judge checked the identical claim and found zero declarations. The declared reason is arguable (a flat prohibition and an all-equal test have no opposite excess) but the check's own falsifier section then describes three independent breaks that give it two independent firing directions, which is what the audit wanted; the exemption looks unnecessary as well as unreported.

items.target: scripts/verify-design.mjs startServer (line 112-129) and JUDGE.md's L1 entry
items.problem: L1 tells a judge that `serve-static exited with 1` is EACCES from the sandbox, is not a broken oracle, and should not be debugged. That instruction is now a hazard, because the message is unconditional on the actual cause and the cause is thrown away. `startServer` spawns the child with `stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore']` - stderr discarded - and its exit handler rejects with the single string `serve-static exited with ${code}` for every non-zero code. I hit it twice this round on the real gate: once sandboxed and once with the sandbox explicitly disabled, which L1's own stated remedy says should have worked. The gate had not run. It then completed 45 checks with 0 failures on a different port and again on the default port, with no change to the tree. Whatever the cause was on those two runs, the harness could not tell me and L1 told me not to look. A judge following L1 literally - and I nearly did - records 'gate green per L1' having never obtained a gate result, which is L2's own failure (a PASS line that is true and worthless) inverted into a FAIL line that is uninformative and dismissible.
items.evidence: scripts/verify-design.mjs lines 113-127 (`stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore']`; `rej(new Error(\`serve-static exited with ${code}\`))`); my own runs this round: two failures at the default port 3111 (one sandboxed, one not) and two clean 45-check / 0-failure completions afterwards, at port 3123 and at the default port; scripts/serve-static.mjs's own exit paths, which exit 1 for a missing root and let a listen error surface uncaught
items.invariant: When the verification harness's server child exits non-zero, the error it raises names the child's own reason - its captured stderr and, where the failure is a listen error, the errno and the port - rather than only its exit code; and JUDGE.md's L1 is amended to say that this message is dismissible ONLY when the harness has printed a cause that is EACCES.
items.prescription: Hypothesis. Change the spawn's stderr from 'ignore' to 'pipe', buffer it, and include the last few lines in the rejection; add an explicit `server.on('error', ...)` in serve-static.mjs that prints `errno` and the port before exiting, so EACCES and EADDRINUSE are distinguishable from each other and from a missing out/. Retry once on the next free port when the errno is EADDRINUSE. Then amend L1 in JUDGE.md, which is append-only for entries but whose entries this loop has amended before: an evidence lie that instructs a judge not to look is only safe while the message it describes has exactly one cause.

items.target: evidence rig (tools/ui-evidence.mjs capture procedure, the /catalog 390 pair specifically)
items.problem: The evidence set's two /catalog 390x844 captures are fullPage PNGs 390 pixels wide and 86,379 pixels tall. At any size a reader or a judge can display them, that is roughly 43 source pixels per displayed pixel: the image resolves to a vertical grey smear carrying no legible content whatsoever. So the two captures covering the surface that holds this loop's largest open reader-facing defect - I23, 396 records at 209.5px each - are the two captures in the set that cannot be read at all. This is a distinct condition from I13 (nothing scroll-linked is observable) and from L5 (a viewport-coupled layout misrenders): here the capture is faithful and correctly labelled and still carries zero information. It has a measurable consequence in this loop's own record: I23 has been carried at impact 5 for four iterations, iter-07's judge wrote that impact 5 is 'almost certainly under-weighted relative to what it does to a real reader', and the reason nobody has revised it is that no judge has ever looked at the surface. I only formed a view this round because I rendered my own 390x844 viewport captures. A rig whose output for one surface is unreadable produces exactly the recall failure D3 describes, and it does so silently.

items.problem: Unchanged. The viewport-coupled fidelity detector is keyed to one CSS signature - an element whose computed position is sticky and whose max-height is vh-based - so it catches the one known case (#catalog-table-wrap at max-height 732.656px, correctly labelled this run) and would not catch a second instance built differently. D9's generalisation is that identity is not fidelity; the detector proves fidelity for exactly one known shape and asserts nothing about any other. I44 is a sibling of this item: a second class of capture the rig accepts without checking whether it carries information.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/manifest.json (only the two /catalog 1440 entries carry capture:'viewport'); JUDGE.md L5
items.invariant: The evidence rig detects a misrendering fullPage capture by comparing the rendered image against the page's live DOM geometry, not by matching a CSS signature: for each capture, at least one measured element's live bounding box agrees with its position in the captured image within a stated tolerance.
items.prescription: Replace the signature match with a differential check: capture at viewport size and at fullPage, measure one high-signal element's box live in each, and label the capture 'viewport' whenever the two disagree beyond tolerance. That detects the class rather than the instance, and it folds into I13's and I44's shared evaluate() call since all three need the same one.
